questions.question: Which of the following disciplines did NOT employ an early form of thematic analysis as described in the text?
True or False: The development of thematic analysis was entirely independent and did not evolve from quantitative content analysis.
Fill in the blank: In the 1980s and 1990s, thematic analysis emerged as a specific approach for analyzing ______ data in fields such as health and the social sciences.
Which of the following statements best reflects the evolution of thematic analysis as described in the text?
options: TA has always been a clearly demarcated method with uniform procedures.
TA was originally used by a single discipline and later adopted broadly.
TA evolved from content analysis, sharing common roots while diverging in methodology and conceptual details.
TA has remained methodologically isolated from other forms of analysis.

questions.question: Which claim accurately captures the methodological challenge associated with different approaches to thematic analysis as outlined in the text?
options: Researchers consistently follow one uniform procedure across all studies of TA.
Divergent procedures and underlying philosophies across approaches like 'coding reliability,' 'codebook,' and 'reflexive TA' can lead to conceptual and methodological conflation.
The existence of multiple approaches indicates mere superficial variations with no real impact on the interpretation of data.
Ignoring philosophical differences in TA ensures methodological unity.
